                    A power saving for planar unit distances
                                                OpenAI

                                          September 23, 2026


                                                Abstract
         We prove a power saving for the planar unit-distance problem: for some absolute β < 4/3,
      every set of n points in the Euclidean plane determines O(nβ ) unordered pairs at unit distance.


1     Introduction
For a finite set X ⊂ R2 , write
                             
                  u(X) = # {x, y} ⊂ X : ∥x − y∥2 = 1 ,              u(n) = max u(X).
                                                                            X⊂R2
                                                                            |X|=n

Thus pairs are unordered and their endpoints are distinct. We prove a fixed power saving over the
exponent 4/3.

Theorem 1.1. There are absolute constants 0 < C < ∞ and 1 ≤ β < 4/3 such that u(n) ≤ Cnβ
for every nonnegative integer n.

    Theorem 1.1 gives a positive answer to the question whether this upper exponent can be
lowered by a fixed amount: equivalently, u(n) = O(n4/3−δ ) for an absolute δ > 0. All constants
are independent of the configuration.

1.1   The unit-distance problem and earlier methods
Erdős introduced the repeated-distance problem in 1946 [10]. Rescaling a configuration turns
any specified positive

INDEX ROW: family 172 | A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations | preprints/A-classification-of-finite-Euclidean-Ramsey-configurations-September-23-2026/paper.pdf
  catalogue abstract: We classify finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations by a necessary and sufficient tensor condition over their coordinate fields. The Ramsey property here concerns monochromatic congruent copies at the original scale under arbitrary finite colorings. The criterion shows that every nonempty subtransitive set and every nonempty set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey. In particular, some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals are not subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the Leader–Russell–Walters conjectured characterization.
  README title: A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations | date: September 23, 2026
-- BY HAND: pdftotext -l 1, first 1400 characters --
    A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
                                              OpenAI

                                       September 23, 2026


                                              Abstract
         We classify finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations by a necessary and sufficient tensor
      condition over their coordinate fields. The Ramsey property here concerns monochromatic
      congruent copies at the original scale under arbitrary finite colorings. The criterion
      shows that every nonempty subtransitive set and every nonempty set of at most five
      points on a circle is Ramsey. In particular, some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals are not
      subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the Leader–Russell–Walters conjectured
      characterization.

build/main.tex :  We classify finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations by a necessary and sufficient tensor condition over their coordinate fields. The Ramsey property here concerns monochromatic congruent copies at the original scale under arbitrary finite colorings. The criterion shows that every nonempty subtransitive set and every nonempty set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey. In particular, some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals are not subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the Leader--Russell--Walters conjectured characterization.

INDEX ROW: family 337 | Sharp integral fillings in CAT(0) spaces | preprints/Sharp-integral-fillings-in-CAT(0)-spaces-September-23-2026/paper.pdf
  catalogue abstract: Every compactly supported integral n-cycle, n ≥ 2, in a proper CAT(0) space bounds a compactly supported integral current with the sharp Euclidean mass bound. The theorem allows arbitrary integer multiplicities and unrestricted ambient dimension. In particular, we prove the Euclidean Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in dimensions at least three.

-- BY HAND: pdftotext -l 1, first 1400 characters --
                    Sharp integral fillings in CAT(0) spaces

                                               OpenAI

                                        September 23, 2026


                                               Abstract
          Every compactly supported integral n-cycle, n ≥ 2, in a proper CAT(0) space bounds a
      compactly supported integral current with the sharp Euclidean mass bound. The theorem
      allows arbitrary integer multiplicities and unrestricted ambient dimension. In particular, we
      prove the Euclidean Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in dimensions at least three.


1    Introduction
The Euclidean isoperimetric inequality bounds the volume enclosed by a boundary of prescribed
area. Its current-theoretic form asks for a filling of a cycle and permits singular supports, integer
multiplicities, and arbitrary codimension. We prove that the sharp Euclidean filling bound holds
in every proper CAT(0) space, in all cycle dimensions at least two.
    Write Ij (X) for the integral j-currents of Ambrosio and Kirchheim [3], ∂ for current boundary,
and M for mass. An integral n-cycle is a current T ∈ In (X) with ∂T = 0; an integral filling is
a current S ∈ In+1 (X) with ∂S = T . A metric space is proper if its closed bounded balls are
compact. A CAT(0) space is a geodesic metric space in which the distance between two points
on a geodesic trian

build/main.tex :  Every compactly supported integral $n$-cycle, $n\ge2$, in a proper CAT(0) space bounds a compactly supported integral current with the sharp Euclidean mass bound. The theorem allows arbitrary integer multiplicities and unrestricted ambient dimension. In particular, we prove the Euclidean Cartan--Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in dimensions at least three.
